title: 생일 초대: 토요일에 우리 집에 오세요
objective: Invite someone with -(으)세요, and accept or politely decline.
summary: A coworker invites friends to his birthday dinner; they accept or decline.
setting: At the office on a Wednesday afternoon. Minsu invites his coworkers Anna and Tom to his birthday dinner at home.

task.title: Invite, accept, and decline
task.line: Read each item, then choose, fill in, put in order, or answer in Korean as asked.

words.meaning: Are you free? (lit. Do you have time?)

words.exampleMeaning: I'm watching a movie in the evening.
My home is in front of the school.
I have plans with a friend today.

words.meaning: I'm sorry (also used before politely saying no)

dialogue.meaning: Anna, are you free on Saturday?

dialogue.korean: 토요일이 제 생일이에요. 저녁에 우리 집에 오세요.
dialogue.meaning: Saturday is my birthday. Please come to my place in the evening.
Wow, sounds great! What time should I come?

dialogue.korean: 여섯 시에 오세요. 톰 씨도 시간 있어요?
dialogue.meaning: Please come at six. Tom, are you free too?

dialogue.korean: 고마워요. 그런데 미안해요. 토요일에 약속이 있어요.
dialogue.meaning: Thank you. But I'm sorry, I already have plans on Saturday.

exercises: Choose the right -(으)세요 form: ① 여기 (앉세요 / 앉으세요). ② 내일 학교에 (가세요 / 가으세요).
Fill in the blank with the -(으)세요 form of 전화하다: 저녁에 저한테 ____.
Your friend asks: 금요일에 같이 영화 봐요? You are busy that day. Choose the better answer: ① 좋아요! 몇 시에 봐요? ② 미안해요. 금요일에 바빠요.
Put the words in order to make an invitation: 오세요 / 일곱 시에 / 우리 집에
Answer in Korean. Say yes and ask what time: 일요일에 같이 점심 먹어요.
answers: 일곱 시에 우리 집에 오세요. (또는: 우리 집에 일곱 시에 오세요.)
좋아요. 몇 시에 만나요? (또는: 좋아요. 몇 시에 먹어요? / 좋아요. 몇 시에 가요?)
